topic.title: Video-Language Representation and Temporal Understanding
topic.overview: Video-language models connect images, motion, subtitles, and descriptions to support retrieval, captioning, and question answering. Unlike an image captioner, a useful video model must track which entities persist, how events unfold, and where relevant evidence occurs. Long videos add a memory and selection problem alongside recognition.
topic.whyItMatters: A model can identify objects yet misunderstand the event sequence or attribute an action to the wrong person. Joint spatial and temporal evaluation helps reveal these failures beyond aggregate caption similarity.
topic.evolution: A 2000 representative uses probabilistic semantic indexing and contextual relations. The 2021 VALUE benchmark broadens evaluation across tasks, while recent work adds reusable video encoders, hour-scale training, and localized spatial-temporal benchmarks. The represented trajectory emphasizes longer contexts and more grounded descriptions, not merely larger collections of independent frames.
openQuestions: How can models retain long-range event structure without losing brief decisive evidence?
Which benchmarks separate genuine temporal understanding from language-based guessing?

papers.title: Comp-Attn: Present-and-Align Attention for Compositional Video Generation
papers.tldr: Comp-Attn improves multi-subject generation by separately strengthening subject presence and aligning attention with their intended relationships.

papers.title: Context Forcing: Consistent Autoregressive Video Generation with Long Context
papers.tldr: Context Forcing combines a long-context teacher with compressed memory to improve consistency in long autoregressive video generation.

papers.title: DiasR: Dual-Modal Identity-Anchored Sparse Routing for Efficient Multi-Subject Video Generation
papers.tldr: DiasR uses identity-aligned representations and sparse subject routing to improve multi-subject video quality and efficiency.

papers.title: E-VAds: An E-commerce Short Videos Understanding Benchmark for MLLMs
papers.tldr: E-VAds introduces a benchmark for dense e-commerce videos and a reinforcement-learning model that improves commercial-intent reasoning with limited training data.

papers.title: Explainable Forensics of Manipulated Segments in Untrimmed Long Videos
papers.tldr: The paper introduces a benchmark and coarse-to-fine system for locating and explaining AI-manipulated segments within otherwise authentic long videos.

papers.title: FlowNar: Scalable Streaming Narration for Long-Form Videos
papers.tldr: FlowNar combines visual context removal with retained streaming memory to improve narration quality and scale to longer videos.

papers.title: FrameOracle: Learning What to See and How Much to See in Videos
papers.tldr: FrameOracle learns which video frames a question requires and adjusts the frame budget to reduce computation while preserving accuracy.

papers.title: LIVEditor-14B: Lightning Unified Video Editing via In-Context Sparse Attention
papers.tldr: LIVEditor-14B uses selective sparse attention to reduce video-editing latency by 60% while preserving visual fidelity in the reported experiments.

papers.title: LoCoT2V-Bench: Benchmarking Long-Form and Complex Text-to-Video Generation
papers.tldr: LoCoT2V-Bench shows that long-video generators struggle more with detailed prompt compliance and character consistency than with visual quality.

papers.title: LOVE: Benchmarking and Evaluating Text-to-Video Generation and Video-to-Text Interpretation
papers.tldr: LOVE combines a human-annotated video benchmark, a multidimensional evaluation metric, and a reinforcement-learning reward that improves video generation.

papers.title: OmniFit: Bridging Modalities via Layer-Adaptive Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: OmniFit compresses tokens according to layer needs and cross-modal alignment, retaining 98% of reported performance with 20% token usage.

papers.title: OmniShow: Unifying Multimodal Conditions for Human-Object Interaction Video Generation
papers.tldr: OmniShow combines text, images, audio, and pose to generate human-object interaction videos and introduces a dedicated evaluation benchmark.

papers.title: OmniSIFT: Modality-Asymmetric Token Compression for Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: OmniSIFT jointly learns video pruning and vision-guided audio selection, delivering strong results with one-quarter of the original token context.

papers.title: PISCES: Annotation-free Text-to-Video Post-Training via Optimal Transport-Aligned Rewards
papers.tldr: PISCES uses optimal-transport-aligned rewards to improve video quality and prompt alignment without human training annotations.

papers.title: Q-CLIP: Unleashing the Power of Vision-Language Models for Video Quality Assessment through Unified Cross-Modal Adaptation
papers.tldr: Q-CLIP uses a small shared visual-textual adapter and quality-level prompts for efficient video quality assessment.

papers.title: Revisiting Uncertainty: On Evidential Learning for Partially Relevant Video Retrieval
papers.tldr: Holmes models uncertainty across videos and within their clips to improve retrieval when a text query describes only partial video content.

papers.title: SegPVSG: Panoptic Video Scene Graph Generation via Temporal Focusing and Generative Augmentation
papers.tldr: SegPVSG improves video relationship recognition by focusing on salient moments and generating contextual training segments for rare relations.

papers.title: T2AV-Compass: Towards Unified Evaluation for Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
papers.tldr: T2AV-Compass jointly evaluates generated audio and video, revealing persistent realism, synchronization, and instruction-following failures across 15 systems.

papers.title: TAGRPO: Boosting GRPO on Image-to-Video Generation with Direct Trajectory Alignment
papers.tldr: TAGRPO improves image-to-video post-training by aligning intermediate latents with high-reward trajectories and separating them from low-reward counterparts.

papers.title: TD-VAD: Breaking Visual Dependence in Video Anomaly Detection with Text-Driven Learning
papers.tldr: TD-VAD learns temporal anomaly patterns from generated text and applies them to video without target-domain anomaly training data.

papers.title: TimeChat-Captioner: Scripting Multi-Scene Videos with Time-Aware and Structural Audio-Visual Captions
papers.tldr: TimeChat-Captioner generates structured, timestamped audio-visual narratives that improve dense captioning and downstream video reasoning and grounding.

papers.title: Towards One-to-Many Temporal Grounding
papers.tldr: A new benchmark, dataset, and training rewards target finding every separate video segment that matches a single text query.

papers.title: V-LynX: Token Interface Alignment for Video+X LLMs
papers.tldr: V-LynX aligns new sensory inputs with a video model's existing token interface using a lightweight pathway and unpaired data.

papers.title: VELR: Efficient Video Reward Feedback via Ensemble Latent Reward Models
papers.tldr: VELR uses ensembles of latent reward models to preserve comparable video reward-learning performance while substantially reducing memory requirements.

papers.title: video-SALMONN S: Memory-Enhanced Streaming Audio-Visual LLM
papers.tldr: video-SALMONN S stores streaming audiovisual experience in model parameters, improving long-video understanding and learning from videos seen hours earlier.

papers.title: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining
papers.tldr: Video2GUI automatically converts Internet tutorials into a large, diverse GUI interaction dataset that improves agent pretraining.

papers.title: VideoLoom: A Video Large Language Model for Joint Spatial-Temporal Understanding
papers.tldr: VideoLoom combines spatial and temporal video understanding with a localized-caption dataset and a benchmark for evaluating both dimensions together.

papers.title: VlogReward: Learning Multi-Dimensional Evaluation for Vlog Editing
papers.tldr: VlogReward evaluates six dimensions of vlog editing and provides actionable feedback using a specialized dataset and modified reward training.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Text-to-Motion Evaluation using Video Language Models
papers.tldr: VeMo evaluates text-motion alignment through rendered videos and pretrained video-language models, correlating better with human judgments than existing metrics.
